description: The earliest Egyptian religion. The gods Ra, Osiris, Isis, Horus, Set, and others are worshipped. The earliest evidence is archaeological (tombs, offerings, early inscriptions).
The Pyramid Texts are inscribed in the pyramids — the earliest surviving religious texts. They describe the king's journey to the sky and his union with the gods.
The 'Contendings of Horus and Set' and other mythic texts are composed. The Book of the Dead begins to take shape.
The Book of the Dead (in its classic form) is used. Amun rises to supreme status (Amun-Ra). The great temples at Karnak and Luxor are built.
The 'Isis cult' spreads across the Mediterranean. The last temple (at Philae) closes in 395 CE under the Roman/Christian empire.
